name: Checkly
description: The code-first reliability platform: synthetic monitoring, uptime monitoring, alerting, and AI-powered incident investigation for APIs, websites, and applications.

skills.name: configure
skills.description: Create and manage monitoring checks, alert channels, dashboards, status pages, and other Checkly constructs using the Checkly CLI.

skills.name: investigate
skills.description: Access check status, analyze failures, trigger on-demand runs, and debug errors across a Checkly monitoring setup.

skills.name: communicate
skills.description: Open and manage incidents and lead customer communications via Checkly status pages.

skills.name: manage
skills.description: Understand a Checkly account's plan, entitlements, feature limits, and available monitoring locations.

when_to_use: Use Checkly when the task is to verify that a deployed API, endpoint, or user journey actually works right now from outside the network; to turn an existing Playwright test suite into production monitoring; to define monitoring as code and deploy it from CI; to get alerted when a cron job or worker stops checking in; to investigate a failing check with traces and AI root cause analysis; or to post and update a public status page during an incident. Checkly is not an APM or a log aggregator: it observes an application the way a customer does and reports when a user-facing path breaks.
best_fit_use_cases: Confirm a deploy did not break a critical user flow, from 22+ global regions.
Run existing Playwright tests as production monitors without rewriting them.
Create, update, and deploy monitors as versioned TypeScript, Terraform, or Pulumi code.
Detect silent failures in cron jobs, scheduled tasks, and background workers.
Get root cause analysis, traces, and logs for a failing check.
Open, update, and resolve incidents on a branded public status page.
not_a_fit_for: Host-level infrastructure metrics and log aggregation (use an APM or observability backend).
Real user monitoring of individual end-user sessions.

cli.write_safety: Write commands (create, update, resolve, deploy) exit with code 2 and a JSON confirmation envelope that an agent must explicitly confirm before the change is applied.
